summary: Fault injection CHG-1c22e75c deliberately stopped redis2, which pushed the 3-node Redis Cluster into a CLUSTERDOWN state with no self-recovery, and go-server's ingestion path fails transactions when its Redis dedup check errors - so throughput has collapsed and the producer is now seeing sustained INTERNAL errors on submission, starving the enricher and the rest of the pipeline of new data.
reasoning: Confirmed well beyond the two-source bar: the timing correlation (change log + redis2's own shutdown log), the explicit server-side error (CLUSTERDOWN), independent Prometheus counters (fraud_server_transactions_total collapsing from ~4/s to ~0.4/s while transaction_errors_total{reason=redis_dedup} climbs from 1 to 297+ at the same instant), and the client-side symptom (python-producer logging 100% gRPC INTERNAL failures). Also checked redis1/redis3 configs to rule out the surviving nodes as contributing (found an unrelated, pre-existing maxmemory inconsistency between them, not causal).
